title: TRACK: Multiple Instance Learning for Anti-Money Laundering in Transaction Networks
abstract: arXiv:2611.06035v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Anti-money laundering (AML) investigations are organized around accounts, while the suspicious evidence for an account may reside in only a few of its transactions. Yet many account-level detectors summarize transactions before learning, and message-passing models may aggregate once more over neighboring accounts. We name this discrepancy the aggregation mismatch and study it under an account-window benchmark label defined by the presence of at least one flagged transaction. We recast account-level AML detection as multiple instance learning, in which an account-window is a bag and its transactions are instances. We propose TRACK, which encodes every transaction with a shared encoder and selectively pools the encodings into an account decision. translated_title: TRACK：面向交易网络反洗钱的多示例学习方法
translated_abstract: 反洗钱（AML）调查以账户为单位组织进行，而一个账户的可疑证据可能仅存在于其少数几笔交易中。然而，许多账户级检测器在学习之前就先对交易进行了汇总，而消息传递模型还可能在相邻账户之间进行二次聚合。我们将这种差异命名为“聚合失配”（aggregation mismatch），并在以“至少存在一笔被标记交易”为定义的账户窗口基准标签下对此展开研究。我们将账户级AML检测重新表述为多示例学习问题：账户窗口作为一个“包”（bag），其交易则作为“示例”（instance）。我们提出了TRACK方法，该方法使用共享编码器对每笔交易进行编码，并有选择地将编码汇聚为账户级决策。为模拟粗粒度监督，我们在整个训练过程中对TRACK隐藏了五个AML数据集的交易标签。在按时间顺序的评估协议下，TRACK取得了最高的平均精度
tldr: 该论文提出TRACK方法，将账户级反洗钱检测重新表述为多示例学习问题，通过共享编码器对每笔交易编码并选择性汇聚为账户决策，从而在无需交易级标签的情况下解决了“聚合失配”问题，并在五个AML数据集上取得了最高的平均精度。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes TRACK, which recasts account-level anti-money laundering detection as multiple instance learning by encoding each transaction with a shared encoder and selectively pooling encodings into an account decision, addressing the "aggregation mismatch" problem and achieving the highest average precision on five AML datasets without transaction-level labels.
